run.notes: CUDA 13 + Python 3.14 bump. Same AMI, instance size, checkpoint and serving flags as 2026-08-19-first-serve-g5g, so the runtime is the only variable. Warm measurements only, single stream, no repeats beyond the 5 timed runs. Result is performance-neutral.

pricing.source: aws ec2 describe-spot-price-history, us-east-1d, g5g.2xlarge, 2026-08-21 (one T4G on this size, so per-chip equals per-instance)

model.architecture_notes: Reference bf16 release, cast to float16 at load. Turing (SM 7.5) has no bf16 datapath and no fp8; the port selects float16 from the live compute capability. The fused W4A16 Pallas kernel is refused at startup here: it needs 550 KiB-1.1 MiB of shared memory per block against Turing's 64 KiB opt-in ceiling.

software.version: jax 0.11.1 / jaxlib 0.11.1 / jax-cuda13-plugin 0.11.1 / jax-cuda13-pjrt 0.11.1 on Python 3.14.6
software.container_image: none (systemd unit on ami-077792d0bb6a000b8, CUDA 13 from pip wheels: nvidia-cublas 13.6.1.10, nvidia-cuda-runtime 13.3.29, nvidia-cudnn-cu13 9.24.0.43)

memory.notes: 13,581 of 15,360 MiB in use while serving (13,573 on 2026-08-19); engine reported 9.26 GB of parameters loaded. kv_cache_gib and resident_kv_tokens are deliberately absent: this engine allocates a static per-sequence cache as ordinary JAX arrays inside XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION=0.90, so there is no engine-managed KV pool. Memory bandwidth was not measured in this run.

startup.notes: Boot to SSM ~35 s. Wheel install ~4 min once apt was working -- but the first attempt wedged 12 min on a 503 from us-east-1.ec2.ports.ubuntu.com; see issues. Weight load 160.4 s cold. First request after init took 18.06 s end-to-end for 53 tokens against 4.50 s warm (4.0x) -- XLA compiling per shape bucket. TTFT was not isolated in this run, so the baseline's 56x prefill ratio was not re-measured. Warm up before recording anything.

cost.notes: Derived from $0.395/hr spot at 11.78 output tok/s sustained single-stream. Higher than the 2026-08-19 figure of $8.54 because of the AZ spot price ($0.395 in us-east-1d vs $0.369 in us-east-1c), not because the runtime got slower -- the decode gauge is flat at 12.4 vs 12.5 tok/s. Single stream only; this engine cannot serve concurrent requests.

issues.summary: apt-get update wedged for 12 minutes at the first bootstrap step. us-east-1.ec2.ports.ubuntu.com returned 503 over IPv4 and resolved to AAAA records only, on a host with no IPv6 address and no IPv6 default route. Not lock contention: apt held the lists lock itself and nothing blocked it, so DPkg::Lock::Timeout did not apply. Canonical ports.ubuntu.com answered 200 in 0.45 s. install.sh now sets Acquire::http::Timeout and Acquire::Retries and falls back to the canonical mirror.

The stall was invisible: get_install_progress reported INSTALL IN PROGRESS for the full 12 minutes with the log mtime frozen, because INSTALL_DONE is the only completion signal and nothing checks for staleness.
Spot capacity refused in us-east-1c and us-east-1b before us-east-1d accepted -- the second consecutive run requiring an AZ walk.

The loader logs 'Loading W4A16 QAT weights into JAX' while serving fp16. Cosmetic but misleading; argv passes --quant-mode fp16 and jax_engine resolves fp16 correctly. Stale log string in the load path.

notes: The CUDA 13 / Python 3.14 bump is performance-neutral. Decode gauge 12.4 tok/s against 12.5 on 2026-08-19; GPU memory +8 MiB; weight load +1.0%. Cite it as currency, not speed.

The end-to-end tok/s rows are NOT a clean comparison against 2026-08-19 and should not be read as a regression: the same prompt produced 53 completion tokens here against 64 there (both finish_reason stop), and usage.prompt_tokens came back 20 against 17. End-to-end wall includes prefill and HTTP, so token count moves it. The decode gauge is the like-for-like number.
Every version predicted by the 2026-08-20 `pip install --dry-run` in tpu.env held exactly on hardware, including the unsuffixed CUDA 13 package naming and the cudnn/nccl exceptions.
The comparison figure of 43.1 tok/s belongs to gpu-vllm-g5g-2b, not to this rig. Directional only -- different instance size, context, concurrency ceiling and a patched Triton kernel.
